daysW2.title: Estella ->  Villamayor de Monjardin
daysW2.short_desc: Wine Fountains and a Cozy Family Stay.
daysW2.long_desc: We started around 9 a.m. from Estella, a charming town with about 28,000 residents. Since we were only walking about 10 kilometers today, we allowed ourselves a later start. The morning was cool, but the temperature kept rising as the day went on. After about 4 kilometers, we reached Bodega Irache, a massive winery famous for its wine fountain, where pilgrims can help themselves to red wine from a tap. Suddenly, Lydia, an American woman from California, said, I’ll take the white wine! She thought the second tap offered white wine,  but it was just water! After a warm uphill stretch, we arrived in Villamayor de Monjardín, where we stayed with Betty and Bert and their two daughters. The family is originally from the Netherlands and has been running their bed and breakfast for two years. They only rent out three rooms, and the house, though old, is wonderfully charming and well-kept. The garden has a lovely, peaceful atmosphere. In the evening, we shared a pilgrim dinner with the family, delicious food and great company. Truly a great place to stay.

daysW2.title: Villamayor de Monjardin -> Torres del Rio
daysW2.short_desc: Routine, Rhythm and a Refreshing Dip in the pool.
daysW2.long_desc: After 9 days on the Camino, life as a pilgrim is starting to settle into a natural rhythm. Wake-up at 6:30 a.m., breakfast at 7:00 a.m.and start walking by 8:00 a.m. Continuing until early afternoon, usually around 1 or 2 p.m. The rest of the day is reserved for rest and sightseeing, leading up to the traditional pilgrim dinner at 7 p.m. The body now follows the trail almost instinctively, with ease and without resistance. Today’s walk to Torres del Río was especially enjoyable. A perfect mix of clouds and sunshine, comfortable temperatures where Navarra showing off its best side. Rolling Basque farmlands and peaceful path made for a calm and satisfying walk. Along the way, we also ran into Cornelia from Casa Rural Montedeio, another familiar face on the Camino. We arrived at Hostel Rural San Andrés shortly after 1 p.m., grabbed a quick bite and then came the highlight of the day, a refreshing dip in the pool. Simple, deserved, and utterly rejuvenating. A perfect end to a day before the Pilgrims dinner.

daysW2.title: Torres del Rio -> Logroño
daysW2.short_desc: Leaving Navarra, entering La Rioja, and looking orward to a rest day.
daysW2.long_desc: After many beautiful km through Navarra, today we crossed into a new region La Rioja, known for its wines, landscapes, and warmth. Our steps felt a bit lighter knowing we were getting closer to one of our key milestoness, the capital city Logroño and a much needed rest day. Crossing a provincial border on the Camino feels symbolic, like closing one chapter and beginning the next. New views, new scents, new encounters and new friends. And tomorrow, no walking boots, heavy backpack, no kilometers. Just rest!

daysW2.title: Logroño - Rest day
daysW2.short_desc: Sun, Tapas, and Rest in the Capital of Wine.
daysW2.long_desc: After 11 days on the trail, it was finally time for something we’d been looking forward to, a well-deserved rest day in Logroño, the sunny and beautiful capital of La Rioja. The day unfolded at a slow and easy pace with some sightseeing, short strolls through the city’s charming streets, a fantastic lunch at TXEBIKO. Later on in the evening, of course, tapas along the famous food street Calle Laurel, where each bar has its own unique specialty. But above all, it was a day for rest and recovery, both body and mind. The city was also starting to prepare for its annual wine festival, and there was a buzz of anticipation in the air. A perfect place to recharge before the next stretch of the Camino.
descriptions_gallery: Lunch with Lee-Anne and Steve from Vancover

daysW2.title: Logroño -> Navarrete
daysW2.short_desc: A Short Walk, a Surprise Swede, and a Magical Altarpiece.
daysW2.long_desc: After two much needed rest days, it was time to lace up our boots again and continue the journey, with Navarrete as today’s destination. With just 13 kilometers ahead, we took the day at a relaxed pace. We call it Walking rest! Leaving Logroño, we passed through a large, beautiful park where several school classes were on their way in, full of laughter, backpacks, and early morning energy. After about 6–7 kilometers, we reached a man-made reservoir, a peaceful spot perfect for a short sun break. But the real highlight came toward the end of the walk. Just before reaching Navarrete, we caught up to a blonde woman with a Swedish flag on her backpack. Naturally, we started talking and it turned out her name was Eva, originally from Varberg, but raised in Brämhult, Borås. Even more surprising, I’ve actually worked a bit with her son, who used to work at Swedavia. Small world! Once in town, we checked into our hotel and were given a lovely room. Navarrete is a charming little town, perfect for a quiet evening. We enjoyed a pilgrim dinner at the hotel and later we visited the local church, known for its impressive altarpiece. By inserting 1 euro into a box, the altarpiece lights up, a simple but almost magical experience that added a touch of wonder to the day.
descriptions_gallery: Iglesia de Santa Maria de la Asunción

daysW2.title: Navarrete-> Nájera
daysW2.short_desc: Vineyards, reunions, and a perfect Camino Day.
daysW2.long_desc: Today’s stage from Navarrete to Nájera offered one of the most enjoyable walks so far. La Rioja’s rolling wine country was in full glory. Sunny skies, temperatures between 23–29°C and a refreshing breeze that made the journey feel effortless. It’s harvest season in Rioja and the vineyards are buzzing with activity. Both machines and manual pickers are busy collecting ripe grapes, and the air is filled with the scents and sounds of a land hard at work. It’s the kind of atmosphere that makes you pause and soak it all in. At a café in Ventosa, we had a joyful reunion with two familiar Camino friends, Ted from Washington D.C. and Douglas from Kuranda in Cairns, Australia. Both are still heading toward Santiago de Compostela, just like us. We’ve also noticed a strong presence of young Spanish pilgrims on the trail, tighter with a great mix of ages and nationalities that brings the Camino to life in a unique way.

daysW2.title: Najera -> Santo Domingo de la Calzada
daysW2.short_desc: From Vineyards to open wheat fields, with raindrops, sunshine and rain again during the pilgrimage.
daysW2.long_desc: Today’s stage from Nájera to Santo Domingo de la Calzada brought a noticeable shift in scenery. We left behind La Rioja’s vineyards and entered wide, open grain fields with a landscape shaped more for farming than winemaking. Sheltered by nearby mountains, the terrain felt calm, expansive, and almost meditative. The day began with a light drizzle and 13°C, but as the hours passed, the sky cleared, and we arrived in Santo Domingo under sunshine and 17°C, a gentle contrast to the morning’s chill. Later during the evening it start to rain, again. We checked into the atmospheric Paradors Hotel Sto Domingo Bernadotte de Fresneda, a historic and peaceful place that added an extra touch of serenity to the day’s end. Along the way, we enjoyed two coffee breaks, perfect in the cool weather and also made new Camino friends, Lisa and Loreen, two young walkers from Frankfurt, traveling with their parents.
